files.description: Shop purchases (900 rows): purchase_id (whole number), subscriber_id (refers to subscribers.csv; most subscribers have several purchases), store_city (city name; the same city is written with different capitals and extra spaces, e.g. "lisbon" and "LISBON"; about 2% empty), quantity (whole number), spend (two decimals).

task_text: For each subscriber, show their first purchase, meaning the one with the lowest purchase_id, with all of its details. `result` should be a table holding one row per subscriber that includes the subscriber_id.
intended_computation: For each of the 302 subscribers return the full purchase row (purchase_id, subscriber_id, store_city, quantity, spend) with the smallest purchase_id.

acceptable_variants.notes: subscriber_id may be the index instead of (or as well as) a column; row order may differ.

predicted_direction.reason: on 3.x the grouping column is no longer passed to the function, so subscriber_id is only in the index; both carry it

notes: Drafted 2026-11-11 in package TASKS_M1; task text, card, naive solution, reference and predicted direction were prepared there.
